questions.prompt: Sort each habit into good practice or bad practice.
questions.explain: Good habits keep secrets and sensitive data out of what the agent can read or send. Bad ones leave them where a prompt can carry them away.

items.text: Paste your API key into the chat so the agent can test the call
items.misconception: A pasted key may be stored or sent, and it ends up in the transcript. Use an environment variable the agent cannot read.

items.text: Keep keys outside the project folder, and add a read-deny rule for any secrets file that has to be there
items.misconception: Keeping secrets out of reach, plus a deny rule as a second layer, reduces the chance of leaking them.

items.text: Copy your whole settings directory into the project so the agent 'has the same setup'
items.misconception: Settings directories often contain keys and tokens. Copy only what is needed.

items.text: Use mock or synthetic data for exercises and tests
items.misconception: Mock data lets you test the workflow without any exposure.

items.text: Point the agent at a folder of sensitive samples to 'get a feel for the data'
items.misconception: Unless your agreement allows processing it that way, the contents may leave your machine.

items.text: Check your data agreement before using an external service on any real data
items.misconception: The agreement decides what is allowed, so check before you send.

questions.prompt: On a shared HPC cluster, sort each action.
questions.explain: Login nodes are shared and storage is governed by policy. Heavy work goes through the scheduler, and you follow the cluster rules.

items.text: Submit the heavy analysis through the scheduler
items.misconception: The scheduler is how shared compute is meant to be used.

items.text: Let an agent run a long heavy computation directly on the login node
items.misconception: Login nodes are shared. Long heavy work there slows everyone down.

items.text: Check whether the cluster allows agents and outbound connections before using one
items.misconception: Policies differ between clusters, so check first.

items.text: Give the agent your SSH private key so it can log in for you
items.misconception: A private key is a credential. Handing it over gives the agent everything you can do.

items.text: Let the agent loop and resubmit jobs without a limit
items.misconception: An unbounded loop can burn your allocation and flood the queue.

questions.prompt: You are not sure if your project's data may be sent to an external model provider. What do you do?
questions.explain: When in doubt, the owner of the agreement decides. Until then, use mock data.

options.text: Ask whoever owns the agreement, and use mock data in the meantime
Assume it is fine because the provider says it does not train on your data
options.misconception: A provider's policy does not replace your project's own agreement.

options.text: Send a small sample to see what happens
options.misconception: A small sample is still a disclosure if it is not allowed.

questions.prompt: A teammate's setup script for an agent. Which line is the problem?
questions.explain: The key is written into a file that will be committed and may be read by the agent. It should come from an environment variable that is not committed.

lines.why: A scratch directory is good practice.
Creating the output directory is harmless.

questions.prompt: You have an unpublished result you would hate to see leaked. You want help from a chat assistant. What is the sensible first step?
questions.explain: Terms and approvals decide what is safe. Your institution's office knows which agreements it has reviewed.

options.text: Ask your research office which tools your institution has reviewed
Paste it into a free consumer chat, since the plan you use is rarely a concern
options.misconception: Consumer plans can allow training use depending on a setting, so the terms matter.

options.text: Remove the title and paste the rest, since nobody could tell whose it is
options.misconception: A result can still be recognised from its content. Removing a title does not change how the text is used.

questions.prompt: What does the Claude Code data usage page say about training on Team, Enterprise and API accounts?
questions.explain: The page says Anthropic does not train on code or prompts under commercial terms unless the customer opts in. It does not replace your own agreement.

options.text: No training on prompts or code under commercial terms, unless the customer opts in
Training always happens, with a retention period of 30 days
options.misconception: The page ties training to consumer settings or customer opt-in. Thirty days is a retention period for commercial accounts.

options.text: Training is controlled by the same personal setting as for Free and Pro accounts
options.misconception: That setting applies to consumer accounts. Commercial accounts follow their terms.

questions.prompt: A reader wants proof they had an idea first. Which habit helps?
questions.explain: A dated public or internal record shows when the work existed.

options.text: Post a preprint or add a dated lab notebook entry
Keep it only in a private chat transcript with an assistant
options.misconception: A chat transcript is not a reliable dated record and may be deleted after the retention period.

options.text: Email it to nobody and trust your memory
options.misconception: Memory carries no date a third party can check.
